title: Java Interface
learningObjectives: Define an interface as a contract that classes can implement.
Declare interface methods and implement them in a class.
Use implements to connect a class to an interface.
Explain that a class can implement multiple interfaces.
Use interface references to write code against capabilities rather than concrete classes.

understand.concept: An interface defines a contract that implementing classes agree to provide. A class uses implements and supplies implementations for the interface's abstract methods. A class can implement multiple interfaces, allowing it to support several capabilities.
understand.whyItMatters: Interfaces separate what callers need from how a class performs the work. They support flexible designs, test doubles and polymorphism across otherwise unrelated classes.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Declare and implement

Declare an interface with `interface`. A class implements it with `implements` and provides concrete implementations of its abstract methods.

## Multiple interfaces

A class can implement more than one interface. This provides multiple capability contracts without multiple class inheritance.

## Interface features

Interface fields are implicitly public, static and final. Interfaces can also contain default and static methods. A class implementing an interface must satisfy its abstract method contracts.

## Common mistakes

- Using extends instead of implements for a class-interface relationship.
- Forgetting a required method implementation.
- Assuming a class can extend multiple classes because it can implement multiple interfaces.

examples.title: Interface static method
examples.code:
interface Unit { static String name() { return "Metric"; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(Unit.name()); } }
examples.explanation: An interface static method is called through the interface name.

questions.prompt: Which keyword connects a class to an interface?
questions.explanation: A class declares the interfaces it implements with implements.

questions.prompt: Can a Java class implement multiple interfaces?
questions.explanation: A class may implement multiple interface contracts.

questions.prompt: What does an interface primarily define?
questions.explanation: Interfaces describe operations implementing classes agree to provide.

questions.prompt: How should an interface abstract method be implemented in a concrete class?
questions.answer: Provide a compatible public method implementation
options: Provide a compatible public method implementation
questions.explanation: Interface abstract methods are public contracts.

questions.prompt: How is an interface static method called?
questions.explanation: Static interface methods belong to the interface itself.
